title: County Boundary Viewer: See the Line
description: View the county boundary around any location with the County Boundary Viewer — click a point, read its county context. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a click on a farm road near a county line shows the boundary itself — and which side of it the farmhouse, the field and the tax bill sit on.
quick_answer: The County Boundary Viewer identifies the county (or county-equivalent) for any location you click or locate, showing the administrative context around the point. Click the map or use your position and read the county — the fastest way to answer 'which county is this in?' with the boundary in view.

faq: Does it show parcel lines?
No — county boundaries, not property parcels. Parcel data is held by counties and assessors in surveyed form; this viewer answers the county question only.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — click anywhere instead; your position is one optional way to place the point.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Boundary datasets update on different cycles and generalise lines at different zooms. The Census framework is the reference the lookup tools here use.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — a located point is used for the answer and not retained.
What is a county-equivalent?
Parishes, boroughs, independent cities and DC — units that function as counties in Census geography. The viewer returns whichever contains your point.
The point is in water.
Counties extend into their waters; the containing unit is still returned — lakes and bays have counties too.
Outside the US?
Equivalent administrative areas abroad are shown as the data's context provides; the full Census treatment is US-shaped.
How zoomed should I be?
Near a line, zoom until the boundary and the roads separate clearly — line work at country zoom is how mistakes are made.
The county name differs from the town's.
Towns straddle and names mislead; the containing polygon is the answer the viewer exists to give.
Can I view several counties at once?
Pan the map — neighbouring boundaries draw with it. The click identifies the one under the point.
